summary: Choose whether a localized mark is baked into portable texture roles, projected as runtime geometry, or reconstructed in a declared runtime shader.
objective: The decal stays registered to its host, changes only intended color, normal or roughness roles, and has an explicit ownership and fallback path.
applies_when: A label, stain, wear patch or damage mark is fixed authoring, replaceable runtime state or a runtime-composited effect.
example_prompts: Bake fixed paint wear while keeping interactive marks replaceable at runtime.
Add runtime warning labels to a Blender-authored machine.
negative_signals: assume Blender shader layers survive core glTF
not_for: A complete high-to-low UV bake workflow.

principles: Bake fixed marks, keep replaceable marks as runtime objects, and allow declared shader compositing outside the checked core glTF path.
Treat color coverage, normal perturbation and roughness change as separate roles; normal and roughness are non-color data.
Projection is directional; curvature, corners and grazing incidence can stretch or clip a patch.
Runtime mesh or shader decals need explicit host identity, state, fallback and cleanup ownership.
implementation: In Blender, name receiver and layer roles; use stable UVs or UV Project, then bake only approved channel contributions.
For runtime projection, export stable receiver identity and store projector position, orientation and size as application state.
Use current DecalGeometry as one tested mesh option; inspect material depth, coverage and corner distortion.
For shader compositing, define coordinates, blends, renderer/backend and fallback rather than claiming automatic core glTF transport.
Dispose owned geometry, material and unshared textures; split, bake or author conforming geometry for unsupported surfaces.
observable_checks: A registration chart stays attached through host transforms and camera orbit.
Color-only, normal-only and roughness-only fixtures affect only the intended response.
Front, oblique, corner and silhouette views expose distortion, clipping and z-fighting.
Add, replace, reset and remove preserve receiver state and release only owned resources.

creative_affordances: Use raised geometry when a badge edge is meaningful.
Bake broad wear and reserve runtime layers for state or annotation.
known_limits: No universal projection offset is prescribed.
Checked core glTF guidance is not a claim about every ecosystem decal extension.
No decal was baked, exported, projected or rendered.

claims.statement: Blender 4.5's UV Project modifier emits a UV map from projector negative Z, can target a chosen UV map and is documented for decals; its perspective-projection limitation states that vertices behind the camera are not properly mapped and suggests subdivision so faces in front of the camera map correctly.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 behavior; not glTF transport or suitability for every receiver.

source_refs.locator: UV Project Modifier; Options: UV Map and Projectors; Usage; Known Limitations: Vertices Behind the Camera

claims.statement: Current Three.js DecalGeometry constructs decal geometry from a receiver Mesh plus projector position, orientation and size, and warns that projection around corners can be distorted.
claims.scope: Current addon documentation; one runtime technique, not a universal implementation.
